title: An Explicit Counterexample to the Rank-Two Poisson Conjecture
summary: Let \[ {\mathcal P}_2={\mathbb C}[x,q,p,z] \] carry the canonical Poisson bracket determined by $ \{p,x\}=\{z,q\}=1 $ and by the vanishing of the other brackets between distinct generators. Here and throughout, ``rank two'' means two canonical pairs in the standard indexing of the canonical Poisson algebras; thus there are four polynomial generators and the Poisson tensor has geometric rank four.
